subject: Regional cloud interruption: customer reroute guidance & post-incident actions
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@helios.ai>, ops@helios.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-12-29T03:12:00Z
Subject: URGENT: Regional cloud interruption — immediate reroute guidance

Hi Samira / Helios ops team,

We’re investigating a targeted infrastructure issue at one of our cloud providers impacting EU and APAC availability zones. Symptoms we’re seeing: elevated 5xx responses from edge connectors, increased request latencies for models hosted in eu-central/asia-southeast, and intermittent connection resets. The US region (us-west, us-east) is unaffected.

What we’ve done (so far):
- Activated automated fallback routing to US pools for affected model variants.
- Disabled a handful of failing edge connectors and warm-started additional US nodes.
- Enabled a temporary lenient routing policy so requests with region hints will be routed to compatible variants in US.

Immediate actions for impacted customers (recommended):
1) If you can tolerate US latency, add a region preference header to API calls: 
   -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "x-rw-region-preference: us"
2) Reduce DNS TTLs to 30s if you rely on our DNS-based edge endpoints (optional but speeds reroute).
3) For session-affine workloads, use the fallback-commands.txt attachment to pin to US endpoints and avoid stale KV cache issues.

Attachments: traffic-reroute-diagram.png (visual), fallback-commands.txt (curl examples + header snippets).

We will keep this thread updated with ETA and a post-incident summary. Please reply with 1) whether you want us to force-override routing for your account, and 2) whether you require a warm standby in US for the remainder of the outage window.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts production traffic. I’m standing by and will escalate to infra leadership as needed.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0194

--
Attachment stubs: fallback-commands.txt (text), traffic-reroute-diagram.png (image)

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@helios.ai>

Subject: Re: URGENT: Regional cloud interruption — immediate reroute guidance

Thanks Diego — we saw the spike in errors on our side and appreciate the quick note. A couple quick Qs: 
1) If we switch region_preference to us, do tokens/sessions remain valid or will we lose KV cache context?
2) Any expected change to rate limits when routed to the fallback US pools? Our throughput patterns are bursty and we want to avoid 429s.

If you can, please force-override routing for Helios for the next 2 hours; latency increase of ~40–80ms is acceptable.

Samira
Platform Lead, Helios AI
samira.khan@helios.ai

On 2029-12-29 03:12, Diego Fernandez wrote:
> We’re investigating a targeted infrastructure issue at one of our cloud providers impacting EU and APAC availability zones.

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@helios.ai>, ops@helios.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-12-30T11:45:00Z
Subject: REG: Regional cloud interruption — post-incident note and next steps

Hi Samira / Helios team —

Post-incident update and short postmortem summary:
Root cause: An upstream networking configuration error at our provider caused asymmetric peering between APAC/EU edge subnets and a subset of storage-backed model hosts. This resulted in connection failures and degraded kv-cache hit rates for EU/APAC traffic.
What we did:
- Manually disabled the misconfigured peering rules and rebalanced traffic to US-hosted pools.
- Warmed additional US capacity and increased temporary rate-limit quota for impacted customers.
- Deployed a config check to fail-fast on similar peering mismatches (automated check added to our CI for edge config).

Customer-facing notes (what you need to know):
- If you already switched to x-rw-region-preference: us you will continue to be routed to US pools; KV context is preserved for API sessions that include the session_id header, but in-flight KV cache state may require a soft-warmup (expect some extra model cold-starts for a short window).
- We increased temporary quota for impacted customers for 6 hours after the incident window to reduce 429 risk; please monitor and tell us if you see throttling.

Attached: postmortem-summary-20291230.pdf (concise RCA) and the prior attachments (reroute diagram + commands).

Next steps for Helios (action items):
1) We enabled forced routing for your account between 2029-12-29T05:10Z and 2029-12-29T07:10Z per request; logs show ~98% traffic successfully routed to US during that window.
2) If you want continued US standby, reach out to your account contact — we can provision a hot standby with guaranteed warm cache for a short term.
3) We’ll schedule a 30-min technical review next week to walk through mitigation and any configuration changes on your side (propose 2029-12-31 09:00 UTC).

We’re also publishing the full postmortem to: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/postmortem-20291230 (link above) and the incident page: https://redwood-internal.example.com/incidents/INC-2029-12-29-17

Apologies again for the disruption and thanks for the quick coordination.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

--
